title: Active probe prioritization and annotation triage playbook
author: Maya Chen
body:
Summary

This playbook defines Redwood's operational policy for: (1) actively prioritizing probe generation and scheduling across workloads, and (2) triaging annotation work to balance latency, budget, and label quality. It covers scoring, caching and de-duplication, annotator assignment rules, TTL/retention, emergency fast-paths, and rollout guidance for changes to probe/annotation policies.

Goals

- Reduce time-to-first-useful-label for high-impact slices to <= 48 hours.
- Keep average annotation cost per labeled probe below budgeted thresholds per workload.
- Maintain annotation quality (agreement with golden set) >= 0.85 for production-critical slices.
- Provide deterministic prioritization so downstream evals and rollouts can depend on probe availability.

Scope and applicability

- Applies to: probe generator services, eval orchestration, probe queueing and the annotation platform (internal and vendor-managed).
- Excludes: long-tail exploratory research probes (> 30k sample pools) which are handled by Research devs under separate budgets.

Definitions

- Probe: a synthetic or live-sampled input produced to exercise model behavior.
- Slice: a user-visible subset of workload (locale, feature flag, API route, model variant).
- Priority Score: numeric score used to order probes for scheduling and annotation.
- Hot Probe: probe with Priority Score >= 85.
- TTL: time-to-live for a probe in the active queue before being demoted or archived.

Priority scoring model

We use a weighted linear score combining business impact, observed drift signal, failure severity, and annotation freshness need. All weights are normalized to sum to 1 in config. Example scoring formula used in the scheduler: 

PriorityScore = 100 * clamp(0,1, w_b*B + w_d*D + w_s*S + w_f*F)

Where: 
- B (business impact) in [0,1] — derived from customer tier, affected revenue routes, or QBR tags.
- D (drift signal) in [0,1] — scaled z-score of recent distribution delta metrics (tokens, intents, embeddings distance).
- S (severity) in [0,1] — failure severity classification from monitoring (0.0 = no failure, 1.0 = P0 user-facing).
- F (freshness need) in [0,1] — how stale labels are for this slice (1.0 means > 90 days or no recent samples).
- clamp() limits to [0,1].

Default weights (runtime config): 
- w_b: 0.40, w_d: 0.25, w_s: 0.25, w_f: 0.10

These are tunable via the eval-scheduler config (see rollout section). The scheduler exposes a REST endpoint /scheduler/score with JSON payload {"slice_id":"...","metrics":{...}}.

Caching, de-duplication, and cluster affinity

- All probes are run through a deterministic fingerprint (sha256 over normalized input + metadata) to avoid duplicate annotation work. Fingerprints are stored in the probe-cache service with a 7-day soft-ttl and 90-day archive index.
- For probes that hit the cache with a valid label and matching label-policy (same gold threshold and annotator-profile), return cached label and do not schedule annotation.
- Cluster affinity: prefer routing probes whose execution context matches cached compute locality to leverage KV-cache priming in the serving runtime (reduces noise in evals for cache-sensitive models).

Annotation triage policy

1) Hot-path (PriorityScore >= 85): 
   - Allocate immediately to high-accuracy annotators (internal pool) with expected turnaround 24-48h.
   - Minimum redundancy: 3 annotators for open-label tasks; 5 for safety-critical slices.
2) Warm-path (60 <= PriorityScore < 85): 
   - Schedule to mixed pool (internal + verified vendors). Redundancy = 3 unless confidence gating applies. Target TTL: 72h.
3) Cold-path (PriorityScore < 60): 
   - Queue to low-cost vendor batches or batched labeling jobs. Redundancy = 1–2. Target TTL: 14 days.

Annotator assignment rules

- Annotator profiles: each annotator has attributes (language, domain_expertise_tags, accuracy_score, max_daily_capacity). Use these to match probes to annotators.
- For slices with user-facing consistency SLOs, require annotator accuracy_score >= 0.9 and domain_expertise_tags to include the slice tag.
- Use stratified assignment to avoid single-annotator bias: ensure no annotator labels > 20% of a slice's hot-path probes in a 7-day window.

Quality gates and consensus rules

- Consensus policy: use majority vote for non-critical slices. Use weighted consensus (weights = annotator accuracy_score) for higher fidelity.
- Golden set calibration: every annotator batch includes 5% golden probes. Annotators falling below expected accuracy incur automatic cooling (suspension) and a retraining workflow.
- Confidence gating: if consensus confidence < 0.6, escalate to adjudicators (senior annotators) and flag slice as "untrusted" for downstream rollouts.

Retention, TTLs, and versioning

- Active queue TTL by path: hot-path 7 days, warm-path 30 days, cold-path 90 days. After TTL expiry, probes are archived and a synthetic resample may be scheduled if the drift signal increases.
- Labels are versioned: label artifacts include annotation_schema_version, annotator_profile_hash, and evaluation-run-id. Use semantic label version tags for rollbacks.

Emergency fast-path (P0 regression)

When monitoring triggers a P0 regression (SLO breach on production slice):
1) Escalate with incident channel #eval-p0 and tag oncall-led-team.
2) Run immediate probe batch generation with minified sample (n=200) covering failing endpoints.
3) Bypass normal scheduling and route to internal adjudicator pool with 24h SLA.
4) Freeze any automated rollouts that depend on the impacted slice until triage completes.

Operational runbook: triage steps

1) Confirm regression and identify affected slice(s) 
   - Query metrics (SLO breach window, error_budget, latency and quality deltas).
   - Command: SELECT slice_id, avg_quality, delta FROM eval_metrics WHERE window_start >= '2026-02-10' ORDER BY delta DESC LIMIT 20;
2) Generate targeted probes (use probe-fab CLI) 
   - Example: probe-fab generate --seed-file s3://probes/failed_examples.csv --slice shipping-confirmation --n 500 --tags p0,fast-path
3) Fingerprint and de-dupe against probe-cache: 
   - curl -X POST https://probe-cache.internal/v1/check -d '{"fingerprints": [...]}';
4) Assign to adjudicator pool and track progress in the triage dashboard.
5) If labels confirm regression, create a rollback plan (see Rollback Checklist) and notify stakeholders.

Metrics and dashboards

Recommended KPIs to track (dashboard tiles):
- Median time-to-first-label (by slice and path). Target cold-path <= 14 days, warm-path <= 72h, hot-path <= 48h.
- Annotation cost per labeled probe (USD) by slice and month.
- Golden-set agreement per annotator and per slice. Thresholds: hot-path >= 0.85.
- Probe queue length and age histogram.
- Fraction of probes served from cache vs new annotation.

Rollout and change control

- Any change to weights in the PriorityScore formula or TTLs requires: 
  1) ADR describing rationale (link to ADR in related_pages),
  2) Canary: run new policy in shadow for 7 days on <= 10% of generated probes,
  3) Metrics gate: no >10% degradation in median time-to-label for hot-path and no >5% drop in golden agreement.
- Deploy config via eval-scheduler config-repo. Example YAML change snippet: 

scheduler_weights:
  w_b: 0.45
  w_d: 0.20
  w_s: 0.25
  w_f: 0.10

Testing and simulation

- Use the probe-simulator service to replay historical workloads with injected drift signals to estimate impact of score/TTL changes. 
- Test plan checklist:
  - Replay 30 days of traffic with 3 drift magnitudes.
  - Validate probe cache hit-rate and estimate annotation cost delta.
  - Run simulated canary and verify metric gates.

Security and privacy controls

- PII scrubbing: probes containing PHI/PII must pass the scrubber pipeline before being queued for annotation. Probes failing scrub must be routed to secure private-labeling and flagged as restricted.
- Access control: annotation artifacts marked restricted can only be viewed by annotators with the "restricted" attribute and by security reviewers.

Ownership and contact matrix

- Policy owner: Applied ML (eval) team (owner: Maya Chen).
- Scheduler service owner: eng-serving-runtime (oncall: runtime-oncall).
- Annotation platform owner: DataOps (oncall: dataops-annotation).
- Escalation path: applied-ml-oncall -> eng-platform -> security if restricted data present.

Appendices

Appendix A — Example scheduler request payload
{
  "slice_id": "checkout-affordability-eu",
  "metrics": {"drift_zscore": 2.3, "recent_failure_rate": 0.12, "gold_coverage_days": 120},
  "metadata": {"customer_tier": "enterprise", "region": "eu-west-1"}
}

Appendix B — Sample SQL queries
- Identify oldest hot-path probes:
  SELECT probe_id, created_at, priority FROM probes WHERE priority >= 85 ORDER BY created_at ASC LIMIT 100;
- Compute average labeling latency by slice: 
  SELECT slice_id, avg(labeled_at - queued_at) as avg_latency FROM labels GROUP BY slice_id;

Appendix C — Change log
- 2025-11-15: Created (Maya Chen).
- 2026-01-10: Weight update proposal (w_b increased to 0.45) and canary tested (Jordan Patel).
- 2026-02-12: Published with final canary results and metric gates (Sofia Alvarez).
